environment: ### Bifrost workspace (org-wide facts — these supersede any generic line above that says None configured, assume private, or no remotes)

**Organization**: A single owner's personal options-trading system (Bifrost) — one human operator, no team. GitHub account `weitingzhao`. Runs as a home lab on LAN 192.168.10.0/24; no public cloud provider.

**Trusted repo**: The workspace root /Users/vision-mac-trader/Desktop/stocks is NOT itself a git repo; it holds 12 sibling git repos, each with remote github.com/weitingzhao/<name>: bifrost-trade-{core,worker,api,frontend,infra}, bifrost-research, bifrost-platform, bifrost-platform-plugin{,-market-data,-flex-query}, bifrost-ui, plus the archived bifrost-analytics (read-only; edits are denied in settings). Also the non-repo dirs backups/ and Research-workspace/. The root-level CLAUDE.md, AGENT_FACTS.md, .claude, .cursor, .mcp.json and scripts are symlinks into bifrost-trade-infra/agent-config/ (the version-controlled governance layer).

**Repository visibility**: PUBLIC — every one of those GitHub repos is public. Anything committed and pushed is world-readable at once; a secret in a commit is a public leak. Only *.example.yaml secret templates and the non-secret Vite env files (bifrost-trade-frontend/.env.development, .env.development.k3s, .env.production) are tracked; every other .env and every real k8s Secret manifest is untracked and must stay so.

**Source control**: GitHub github.com/weitingzhao/* (public; default branch `main` everywhere; the owner commits directly to main; branch protection unknown) plus an in-cluster Gitea mirror gitea.cicd.svc.cluster.local:3000/bifrost/<repo> (NodePort 192.168.10.73:30300) that is written only by the `mirror-sync` step of the deliver pipelines and never pushed to by hand. A push to main is a deploy trigger in two cases: the Argo CD apps `bifrost-platform-stg` and `bifrost-platform-prod` auto-sync (prune + selfHeal) from bifrost-trade-infra main, and `bifrost-research` auto-syncs from bifrost-research main — so a push there changes running STG/PROD. The `bifrost-stg` and `bifrost-prod` Argo apps are manual-sync.

**Cloud provider(s)**: None. Everything is self-hosted on the K3s cluster `bifrost-bootstrap` (apiserver https://192.168.10.73:6443, kubeconfig ~/.kube/bifrost-k3s.yaml; the default kubectl context `docker-desktop` is NOT this cluster).
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None — no wiki, gist or paste service is trusted; GitHub itself is public.

**Secrets management**: Plain files, no vault. Per-repo untracked .env files (bifrost-platform/.env + .env.local, bifrost-research/.env, bifrost-platform-plugin*/.env, bifrost-trade-infra/.env, bifrost-trade-frontend/.env.development.local), untracked k8s Secret YAMLs applied by hand from the *.example.yaml templates (k8s/base/secrets, k8s/data/secrets, k8s/cicd/gitea/secret.yaml, k8s/overlays/*/…token*.yaml), ~/.kube/bifrost-k3s.yaml (cluster-admin), and MCP tokens injected as ${PLATFORM_OPERATOR_TOKEN} / ${PLATFORM_VIEWER_TOKEN} env expansions in .mcp.json. IB/TWS logins happen only inside the TWS software on the two Win11 machines (owner-typed, 2FA) and exist nowhere in this workspace or cluster.

**Default / protected branches**: `main` in every repo; the owner is the only committer and pushes to main directly, so push-to-main is not routine — for bifrost-trade-infra and bifrost-research it is a release action (see Source control) and must be explicitly asked for.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: Tekton in namespace `cicd`: bifrost-ci-{frontend,platform,python} (Gitea push webhooks), bifrost-deliver-stg / bifrost-deliver-prod (Trade), bifrost-deliver-platform / bifrost-deliver-platform-prod (Ops), bifrost-deliver-research, bifrost-build-*, bifrost-smoke. Images go to the in-cluster registry registry.cicd.svc.cluster.local:5000 (NodePort 192.168.10.73:30500); Kaniko builds in-cluster (no local Docker). Argo CD (namespace cicd) applies bifrost-trade-infra overlays. PROD manifests change through git + Argo sync (MCP gitops_sync_app); `kubectl apply` on prod overlays strips Argo tracking and is wrong even when it works. Release order is STG first, PROD only after the release gate; Promote mode starts read-only.

**Network posture**: Home LAN 192.168.10.0/24 behind a UniFi UCG Max (zone-based firewall, IDS/IPS, VLANs 10/20/30/50; managed only via platform-api executors and scripts/unifi_firewall_setup.py — spine D9 — never via ad-hoc UniFi UI or Integration-API-key writes). kube-vip VIP 192.168.10.100 fronts trader.bifrost.lan / stg.trader.bifrost.lan / dev.trader.bifrost.lan / ops.bifrost.lan / stg.ops.bifrost.lan. This Mac has open internet; the cluster nodes are LAN-only. K3s nodes: ubt-k3s-02 = mini-pc-a 192.168.10.70 (workload-pool prod-pool — the PROD node), ubt-k3s-01 = mini-pc-c 192.168.10.73 (control plane, monitoring, Tekton; the NodePort address used everywhere), ubt-k3s-04 192.168.10.75 (data-primary: CloudNativePG), ubt-k3s-05 192.168.10.77 and ubt-k3s-06 192.168.10.79 (general pool), gpu-server 192.168.10.60 (compute pool: RTX 4090, Ollama, MinIO, heavy Tekton). Off-cluster: two Win11 TWS machines (IB Host + Secondary; never scheduled into K3s; reached only over the IB API socket), Mac minis 192.168.10.50 / .52 (agent hosts), a NAS at 192.168.10.20 (archive and backup target), and this MacBook (kubectl + MCP client + Vite dev).

**Host containment**: This is the owner's ordinary macOS workstation (user vision-mac-trader), not a sandbox or CI runner. It holds the cluster-admin kubeconfig, every .env secret and a PROD database dump, so "local" does not mean "harmless".

**Trusted internal domains**: 192.168.10.0/24 (all hosts above), *.bifrost.lan, *.svc.cluster.local, 127.0.0.1 / localhost. Trade gateways on 192.168.10.73: :30880 = PROD, :30881 = STG, :30882 = DEV (the DEV inner-loop API behind Vite :5173); Ops Console/API NodePorts :30876–:30879; registry :30500; Gitea :30300; apiserver :6443. Local dev ports (tmux session `bifrost`, managed by `bdev`): platform-api 8780, platform-console 5180, git-bridge 8785, probe-bridge 8786, trade-ui 5173, prometheus-pf 9090. GitHub (github.com, api.github.com) and the public package registries (npmjs, PyPI) are the only routine external endpoints; api.deepseek.com and the Polygon market-data API are provider endpoints for their own keys.

**Trusted cloud buckets**: MinIO only (S3-compatible, in-cluster, LAN-only). Service minio in namespace `data` (minio.data.svc.cluster.local:9000) holds bucket s3://bifrost-postgres-backup/ — the CloudNativePG Barman backup + WAL store for cluster `bifrost-postgres` (namespace data, 2 instances). A second MinIO in namespace `data-warehouse` (on gpu-server) is the Research / Golden Source object store. Both are operator-owned stores, not upload targets for arbitrary local data; deleting or rewriting objects in the backup bucket destroys the database's point-in-time recovery.

**Key internal services**: platform-api :8780 (Ops control plane; the spine `GET /api/v1/context` is the authority on decisions D1–D13; the MCP servers bifrost-platform / bifrost-kubernetes are operator-role bridges to it, bifrost-redis / bifrost-postgres / bifrost-prometheus are viewer-role read-only bridges, bifrost-trade-api is a read-only Trade gateway bridge); platform-console :5180; Trade API deployments monitor / account / market / research per env namespace (bifrost-dev / bifrost-stg / bifrost-prod); CloudNativePG cluster bifrost-postgres in `data` hosting bifrost_dev, bifrost_stg, bifrost_prod and the Research OLAP db bifrost_golden_source; Redis: redis-live + redis-queue per env, and redis-ib in `data` = the shared live IB event bus fed by the Platform IB Gateway plugin, which is the only component that talks to TWS (IB API socket, client ids 70/71 Host and 72/73 Secondary; its operator command stream may be written only by the Daemon — see the D10 line below); research-api :8795 + research-mcp + Dagster in `research`; market-data plugin :8790 and flex-query plugin :8791; kube-prometheus-stack (Prometheus / Alertmanager / Grafana) in `monitoring`, Alertmanager routing Bifrost* alerts to the ops-agent webhook; Ollama in `ai`; Gitea / Argo CD / Tekton / registry in `cicd`.

**Internal package registry**: None — npm and PyPI are the public upstreams; `@bifrost/ui` is consumed as a local link from ../bifrost-ui; Python cross-repo deps pin BIFROST_CORE_REF git refs. Container images live only in the in-cluster registry.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: (1) backups/bifrost_prod_pre_p9_20260730T230317Z.dump (+ .sha256) — a full PROD database dump with the owner's real brokerage positions and trades; (2) every untracked .env and real k8s Secret YAML listed under Secrets management; (3) ~/.kube/bifrost-k3s.yaml and ~/.bifrost-dev/; (4) the CONTENTS of the databases bifrost_prod / bifrost_stg / bifrost_dev / bifrost_golden_source and of redis-ib — positions, executions, P&L, order intents; (5) IB Flex query tokens and Polygon / DeepSeek API keys. The IB account ids themselves (U17123565 = Host, U8829175 = Secondary) are identifiers, not secrets: they may appear in UI, logs and docs, because IB logins happen only inside TWS on the two Win11 machines and no IB password exists in this workspace or cluster. Audience for the items above: the owner only, on this machine and inside the LAN. Never commit, push, paste, upload or summarise raw contents of them into GitHub (public), gists, issue trackers, chat, or any external API.

**Data retention / declassification**: PROD → DEV/STG data refresh is an owner-gated clone (MCP trigger_data_clone; target bifrost_dev or bifrost_stg only; bifrost_prod is a source, never a target). CNPG backups follow bifrost-trade-infra/docs/GOLDEN_SOURCE_RETENTION.md. Nothing is ever declassified for external sharing.

**Sensitive remote targets**: namespaces bifrost-prod and bifrost-platform-prod (PROD), `data` (the single CNPG cluster holds PROD's database, plus redis-ib), `cicd` (Gitea mirror, Argo CD, Tekton, registry — the shared release machinery), `monitoring`; node mini-pc-a / ubt-k3s-02 / 192.168.10.70 (PROD placement); the two TWS Win11 machines and redis-ib (the live broker path); the UCG Max controller and its firewall zones; the NAS 192.168.10.20; MinIO bucket bifrost-postgres-backup; the Argo apps bifrost-prod / bifrost-platform-prod; the Tekton pipelines bifrost-deliver-prod / bifrost-deliver-platform-prod. STG (bifrost-stg, bifrost-platform-stg) is the release-gate environment: shared, but a deliberate deploy target once the owner asks.

**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: bifrost-prod, bifrost-platform-prod, data, cicd, monitoring — writes there (kubectl apply / patch / delete / scale / rollout / exec, Argo sync or rollback, pipeline runs targeting prod, node cordon / drain / poweroff / wake) need the owner's explicit go for that specific action. bifrost-dev and the plugin-* namespaces are the working environments; the DEV inner loop (Vite :5173 against :30882) is where UI changes are accepted.

**Protected IaC scopes**: bifrost-trade-infra/k8s/overlays/prod/** and overlays/platform-prod/** (PROD placement, secrets patches, daemon-observe-safe), overlays/stg/daemon-scale-zero.patch.yaml (D10 guard), k8s/data/** (CloudNativePG cluster, backups), k8s/cicd/** (Gitea, Argo CD, Tekton, RBAC, triggers / webhooks), k8s/monitoring/** (PrometheusRules / Alertmanager — apply only via `kubectl apply -k k8s/monitoring`), k8s/base-platform/** and any RBAC / ServiceAccount / NetworkPolicy / quota object; the agent governance layer bifrost-trade-infra/agent-config/** (CLAUDE.md, AGENT_FACTS.md, scripts/agent-guard/preflight.js, claude/settings.json, cursor/hooks.json — Cursor/Claude parity is mandatory and the guard is never weakened to get past a block); bifrost-platform/config/ops-context.yaml (the spine: decisions belong to the owner, an agent never flips a status); UniFi firewall zones / policies / IDS settings.
### Owner-specific

**Primary use of Claude Code**: Software development and operations of the Bifrost system in four declared agent modes — Product (bifrost-trade-frontend UI, Dense UI, accepted on the local Vite :5173 DEV inner loop), Ops (bifrost-platform + bifrost-trade-infra: K3s, spine, release gates, CI/CD), Promote (release / cutover assessment, read-only first, releases only on the owner's explicit instruction), Research (bifrost-research dbt / OLAP; writes only dw_stock.* / features.*, never the Trade DB or raw_market.* ingest — spine D13). Conversation is in Chinese; UI strings and identifiers are English. Claude Desktop sessions are filed under the groups `Trade. System` and `Ops - Plugin`; both start in /Users/vision-mac-trader/Desktop/stocks and therefore share this configuration, the hooks and the memory directory.

**Hard boundary D10 (trade-execution freeze, spine status BLOCKED)**: live order placement, daemon auto-trade scale-up (the daemon Deployment stays replicas: 0 in STG and observe-safe in PROD), S08 execution wiring to the Gateway RPC, arming via Monitor POST /api/monitor/control/*, and any write to the redis-ib stream ib:operator:cmd are forbidden in every mode. It is enforced mechanically by scripts/agent-guard/preflight.js (a PreToolUse hook on Bash / Edit / Write / MCP calls) which reads the spine at run time; unlocking needs the owner's explicit written instruction AND spine decision D10 set to UNLOCKED — until then these rules cannot be cleared by any in-session intent.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `bdev` (tmux dev-session manager declared in ~/.bifrost-dev/sessions.yaml: platform-api, platform-console, prometheus-pf, git-bridge, probe-bridge, trade-ui — the only sanctioned way to start / stop / restart local services; never run the whole-package scripts/run_platform.py, start.sh or run-local-ui.sh alongside it, never `kill` / `pkill` its processes, never leave a bare `kubectl port-forward …9090`); `make` targets in bifrost-trade-infra (k3s-*, check-agent-parity) and in the Python repos (lint / test); `kubectl` against ~/.kube/bifrost-k3s.yaml; `gh` as weitingzhao; the six bifrost-* MCP servers (prefer their read tools over shell); `npm run dev:k3s | lint | build | test:run | check:legacy-css | check:code-health` in bifrost-trade-frontend; `claude` itself.

**Routine work**: editing, linting, testing and building inside the workspace repos; reading cluster state (kubectl get / describe / logs, MCP get_* / list_* / query_prometheus); curl GET against LAN / localhost health and API endpoints; bdev status / logs / restart; git commit on main when the owner asked for the change; driving the DEV UI at 127.0.0.1:5173 in the in-app browser; writing memory notes under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-vision-mac-trader-Desktop-stocks/memory/.
allow: Cluster Read-Only Inspection: `kubectl get / describe / logs / top / explain / api-resources / config view`, `kubectl diff`, `--dry-run=client|server`, `kubectl kustomize`, Prometheus / PromQL queries, Argo / Tekton status reads, and the bifrost-* MCP get_* / list_* / query_* / verify_* / platform_mcp_health tools against the K3s cluster — any namespace, PROD included; reading is how every decision here starts. Not `kubectl exec`, and no port-forward other than the sanctioned bdev prometheus-pf.

LAN Health Probes: `curl` / HTTP GET or HEAD requests to 127.0.0.1, 192.168.10.0/24 NodePorts, *.bifrost.lan and *.svc.cluster.local endpoints (health, status, /api/v1/context, the DEV / STG / PROD gateways) to observe state.

Local Dev Services via bdev: `bdev status | logs | start | stop | restart <name>` and the MCP list_dev_sessions / restart_dev_session / get_dev_session_logs — the owner-mandated way to manage the tmux dev session; `npm run dev:k3s` for the Vite DEV inner loop on :5173 and driving that page in the in-app browser.

Repo Quality Gates: `npm run lint | build | test:run | check:legacy-css | check:code-health`, `npx vitest`, `npx tsc`, `npx eslint`, `make lint | test`, `go build ./... && go test ./...`, `bash scripts/check-agent-config-parity.sh`, `node scripts/agent-guard/test.js`, pre-commit hooks — run freely and repeatedly.

Workspace Git Commits: `git add` / `git commit` in any of the 12 workspace repos on the branch the owner is working on (they work on main) when the change was asked for; `git -C <sibling repo>` read and commit operations across the sibling repos — the workspace is one system split into repos, moving between them is not scope escalation. Pushing stays under the push rules below.

Gitignored Local Settings: editing ~/.claude/settings.json, the gitignored bifrost-trade-infra/agent-config/claude/settings.local.json and ~/.bifrost-dev/sessions.yaml when the owner asked for that configuration change — never to weaken the preflight guard, the hook wiring in claude/settings.json or cursor/hooks.json, or these auto-mode rules in order to get past a block.
soft_deny: Protected-Namespace Writes: any state-changing kubectl (`apply`, `patch`, `edit`, `delete`, `scale`, `rollout`, `exec`, `cp`, `label` / `annotate` on live objects, `create secret`), the MCP tools scale_deployment / rollout_restart_deployment / delete_pod / gitops_sync_app / gitops_rollback_app / start_pipeline_run / delete_pipeline_run / stack_install_addon / stack_upgrade_addon / ensure_*, or Argo / Tekton actions targeting bifrost-prod, bifrost-platform-prod, data, cicd or monitoring — and likewise bifrost-stg / bifrost-platform-stg, the release-gate environment. Each needs the owner's explicit instruction for that action in this session (a STG release is normally asked for as 先发 STG). `kubectl apply -f` on anything under k8s/overlays/prod or overlays/platform-prod is wrong even with intent: PROD changes go through git + Argo sync.

Node Lifecycle: `kubectl cordon | uncordon | drain | taint`, `kubectl delete node`, the MCP tools cordon_node / uncordon_node / drain_node / poweroff_compute_node / wake_compute_node / join_cluster_node, and ssh / Wake-on-LAN / poweroff commands against 192.168.10.60 / .70 / .73 / .75 / .77 / .79, the NAS .20 or the Mac minis — cluster capacity and the PROD node are the owner's call; propose first.

Database & Backup Operations: MCP trigger_cnpg_backup / repair_cnpg_wal_store / trigger_data_clone, `pg_dump`, `pg_restore`, `psql` DML / DDL against bifrost_prod / bifrost_stg / bifrost_golden_source, DDL in any Trade DB (schema changes are documented in bifrost-trade-core/docs/DATABASE.md and applied to all three envs on the owner's go), `redis-cli` writes (SET / DEL / FLUSH* / XADD / XTRIM / CONFIG) against redis-ib, redis-live or redis-queue, deleting or rewriting objects in s3://bifrost-postgres-backup/, and deleting or moving backups/*.dump — all destructive to the trading record or its recovery path.

Release & Promotion: starting bifrost-deliver-stg / bifrost-deliver-prod / bifrost-deliver-platform* / bifrost-deliver-research runs, moving the `prod` image tag, Argo syncs of bifrost-prod / bifrost-platform-prod / bifrost-research, running the release gate with an admin token, or bumping k8s image tags in bifrost-research/k8s (auto-synced) — Promote mode assesses read-only first; a release happens only when the owner says so for that environment, STG before PROD, and never with a manifest bump before the image exists in the registry.

Governance & Guard Edits: modifying bifrost-trade-infra/agent-config/** (CLAUDE.md, AGENT_FACTS.md, .mcp.json, claude/settings.json hooks, cursor/hooks.json, scripts/agent-guard/*, claude/auto-mode/*), bifrost-platform/config/ops-context.yaml decisions or statuses, the console governance catalogs (agentProtocolCatalog.ts FORBIDDEN_ACTIONS / AGENT_MODES), the D10 guard patch files, or the Cursor / Claude parity-tracked rule files without bumping parity-id — these are the owner's control surfaces; change only on explicit instruction, both sides in sync, parity script green.

Public Repo Pushes: `git push` to any github.com/weitingzhao/* repo — all are PUBLIC and, for bifrost-trade-infra and bifrost-research, main is auto-deployed by Argo CD. Push only when the owner asks for the push (or for the release that implies it), never with untracked .env / secret / dump files staged, and never force-push or delete remote branches or tags.

Network Controller Changes: any UniFi / UCG change — firewall zones, policies, VLANs, SSIDs, port profiles, IDS/IPS, Default Security Posture, API keys — outside the platform-api executors and the scripts/unifi_firewall_setup.py audit path (spine D9). Manual UI or Integration-API-key writes are forbidden in every mode; executor-driven changes need the owner's explicit go.

Local Runtime Hygiene: starting scripts/run_platform.py, start.sh, run-local-ui.sh, run_frontend.sh, run_backend.sh or any other whole-package runner outside bdev; `kill` / `pkill` of the platform-api, platform-console, git-bridge, probe-bridge, trade-ui or prometheus-pf processes; leaving a manual `kubectl port-forward … 9090`; editing ~/.bifrost-dev/sessions.yaml unasked; running the retired bifrost-trade-socket processes or any Celery / Flower runtime (both retired — double-writing the IB bus is an incident).

Cross-Domain Writes (spine D13): code or SQL that makes bifrost-research write to a Trade database or to raw_market.* ingest tables, makes bifrost-platform know Trade-specific concepts (Greeks, IB protocol, SEPA, straddles, daemon strategy), makes a Trade repo modify platform-api routes or Ops Console architecture pages, or edits the archived bifrost-analytics / bifrost-trader-engine — architectural boundaries the owner set; raise it as a question, do not do it.

Interface & Schema Changes: changing a public interface in bifrost-trade-core without bumping pyproject.toml in the same change, adding a new RPC / external dependency / table or column, or deleting a Research API field in one step — architecture-level decisions; present 2–3 options and wait for the owner (CLAUDE.md §5).
hard_deny: D10 Trade-Execution Freeze: while spine decision D10 is BLOCKED (it is), never: scale the `daemon` Deployment above 0 in bifrost-stg or bifrost-prod (kubectl scale / patch / edit or MCP scale_deployment); remove, move, truncate, rewrite or bypass k8s/overlays/stg/daemon-scale-zero.patch.yaml or k8s/overlays/prod/daemon-observe-safe.patch.yaml; wire S08 daemon execution or a live place_order path to the Gateway RPC; POST / PUT / DELETE /api/monitor/control/* on any environment; write (XADD / LPUSH / RPUSH / PUBLISH / SET / HSET / DEL / XTRIM) the redis-ib stream ib:operator:cmd; place, modify or cancel real orders or hedges through TWS / IB; or push a change whose main purpose is enabling live order placement. Reading these (XLEN, GET /control/status, cat the patch files) is fine. No in-session instruction clears this — only the owner's written unlock together with the spine status change, after which this rule is edited out.

PROD Database as a Target: never clone, restore, `pg_restore`, `psql -f`, TRUNCATE, DROP or run migrations into bifrost_prod from any source, and never point trigger_data_clone at it — PROD is a source only (agentProtocolCatalog FORBIDDEN_ACTIONS, all modes).

Guard Tampering: never disable, edit around, skip (`--no-verify`, removing hook entries, `git config core.hooksPath`), or race scripts/agent-guard/preflight.js, the PreToolUse / Stop hook wiring in claude/settings.json or cursor/hooks.json, the husky / pre-commit code-health gates, Cursor / Claude parity, the spine's D10 status, or this auto-mode configuration in order to get an action through — report the block to the owner instead.

Exfiltration of Owner Data: never commit, push (all repos are PUBLIC), upload, paste, email, post or send to any external API the contents of backups/*.dump, any .env / k8s Secret / kubeconfig / token file, database rows from bifrost_* or bifrost_golden_source, redis-ib payloads, account contents (positions, executions, P&L), or Polygon / DeepSeek / IB Flex credentials — not even "just a sample", and not to a service the owner also uses. Bare IB account ids are not in this list.

Firewall Posture: never toggle the UCG Default Security Posture (Allow All ↔ Block All), disable IDS/IPS, bulk-delete Bifrost firewall zones or policies, or write through the UniFi Integration API key path on the controller — the network is the perimeter protecting the broker path (FORBIDDEN_ACTIONS, all modes).
